title: Senior Flutter Developer
description:
Daxko builds the software that powers fitness, wellness, and community organizations—everything from member management and payments to digital engagement and analytics. From small studios to the largest associations, we help thousands of fitness businesses streamline operations, enhance member experiences, and drive sustainable revenue growth.
  
  
**You'll join Grip Technologies Pvt. Ltd., a Daxko subsidiary, working on FitnessForce, the club management platform used by gyms and fitness businesses around the world.**
**About The Role**
FitnessForce's mobile ecosystem includes two apps: a whitelabeled member app for bookings, subscriptions, and workout tracking, and a business app that runs daily club operations for staff. As a senior Flutter developer, you'll own both, building secure, high-conversion mobile experiences that sync in real time with our .NET Core backend.
  
  
You'll use AI coding tools like Cursor to move faster, while keeping the codebase clean, performant, and maintainable across iOS and Android.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Architect and maintain a single codebase that powers dozens of regional whitelabel clients, managing build-time flavor configurations through CI/CD pipelines like Fastlane
* Integrate secure payment SDKs such as Stripe, building Apple Pay and Google Pay checkout flows for retail purchases and subscriptions
* Drive feature delivery across both the member app and staff app, working through complex logic for POS, multi-club access, and real-time scheduling
* Implement Clean Architecture and state management patterns like Bloc or Riverpod to handle complex, asynchronous UI states
* Manage network layers with Retrofit and maintain reliable code-generation workflows for stable, conflict-free builds
* Champion automated testing across unit, widget, and integration levels to keep releases reliable
* Profile and optimize app performance for large datasets, keeping rendering smooth and memory use efficient across devices

**What You'll Bring**

* 6 to 8 years of software engineering experience, including at least 4 years with Flutter and Dart in production
* Experience building multi-tenant or white labeled mobile apps from a single codebase, with familiarity deploying to the App Store and Google Play
* Hands-on experience integrating native payment SDKs and mobile wallets, including handling 3D Secure authentication and transaction errors
* Experience using AI coding assistants in production, with the Dart and Flutter fundamentals to keep AI-assisted code performant and maintainable
* Strong understanding of mobile system design, state management, and dependency injection
* Working knowledge of native iOS (Swift or Objective-C) and Android (Kotlin or Java) for platform channels and native integrations

**Nice to have**

* Experience in the fitness, wellness, or club management software industry
* Understanding of event-driven backend architectures like Kafka, to align mobile caching with backend data streams

title: Edge Platform & Deployment Engineer
description:
**Type:**
Full- time
  
  
**Experience:**
1 - 3 Years
  
  
**Location:**
Mumbai
  
  
**About The Role**
You own the stack that sits on the plant floor, and you grow it. Our edge gateway runs on a Linux box in a control panel. It talks to PLCs, CNCs and meters on one side and to our cloud on the other, and it has to keep doing that unattended for months. Every protocol we support is a separate installable app, and the list keeps growing: whenever a customer brings a controller we don't speak yet, you build the adapter for it.
  
  
This is partly a product role. Most people who use what you build won't be engineers: plant operators, maintenance teams, our solutions and support staff, and partners setting up their own sites. You decide what gets built and how it works, so that someone who has never heard of a register map or a system unit can still configure a device, add tags, and know whether their data is healthy. If a feature only works when you're the one using it, it isn't finished.
  
  
One morning you might be tracing a bad RS-485 cable on site. That afternoon you might be wrapping a vendor's C library for a new CNC, or redesigning a setup screen because a technician got stuck on it. You maintain the platform, extend it, shape it, and personally get it running on real devices at real sites.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Decide what the platform should do next. Turn field problems, support tickets and customer requests into features, set priorities, and make the trade-offs between power, simplicity and reliability.
* Design for people unfamiliar with the tech:

– Guided setup with defaults that work, plain-language errors, and validation that catches mistakes before they reach a device
  
  
– Status and health that a non-engineer can read at a glance
  
  
– Configuration that can't silently break something.
  
  

* Watch real users set up and run the product, find where they get stuck or need to call us, and remove those steps.
* Build new protocol apps to extend the ecosystem: take a protocol or controller we don't support yet, find the best library or vendor SDK for it, and ship a production adapter that follows our app contract (polling, packaging, install scripts, configurator, monitoring), so that every new protocol is just as easy to set up as the existing ones.
* Pick the right language for each job. Today the platform runs on Node.js, Python, C++, TypeScript and Bash, and the next adapter might need C#, Go, Java or Rust if that's where the only solid driver lives.
* Commission edge gateways at customer sites: install the device, configure the network, connect it to the PLCs, SCADA, DCS or meters, onboard it to the cloud, and confirm the data is right, not just that it's flowing.
* Read the existing OT setup before touching it: identify the assets, controllers, protocols, register and tag maps, network layout, and who owns what.
* Configure and troubleshoot the existing adapters (Modbus TCP/RTU, OPC UA, Siemens S7, Omron FINS, Mitsubishi MC, Fanuc FOCAS) and validate every value against the source.
* Maintain the core platform: the orchestrator and its web UI, the configurator, the install and uninstall scripts, and the data pipelines (Redpanda/Kafka, MQTT, HTTP).
* Own releases end to end: build, package, version, ship, and roll out to devices in the field without breaking any that are already live.
* Diagnose failures remotely and on site using logs, metrics, VPN, SSH and packet captures, then fix the root cause, not just the symptom.
* Keep deployments secure by default: segmented networks, least privilege, managed secrets, and read-only access to controllers unless writes are explicitly approved.
* Write the user guides, runbooks and site documentation that let others deploy and run the product without you.

**What We're Looking For**

* Engineering degree. Mandatory. Instrumentation, Electrical, Electronics, Computer Science, or equivalent.
* 1 - 3 years in industrial automation, IIoT, OT integration, systems engineering, or a field-facing technical role.
* Product sense:

– You think about who will use a feature before you think about how to build it
  
  
– You can explain a technical constraint in plain language
  
  
– You'll cut a clever option if it confuses the person on site
  
  

* A generalist engineer, not a one-language developer:

– You can pick up an unfamiliar codebase or language and be productive in it quickly
  
  
– You choose tools by what the job needs (library maturity, vendor support, performance, how it deploys on an edge box), not by habit
  
  
– You're comfortable reading C headers, vendor SDK docs and protocol specs to work out what a driver actually does.
  
  

* OT fundamentals you can apply on site:

– PLCs, SCADA, DCS and historians: what each does and where data really lives
  
  
– Industrial sensors, transmitters and energy meters
  
  
– Digital and analog I/O: 4–20 mA, 0–10 V, scaling, dry and wet contacts
  
  
– Serial wiring and RS-485 multidrop
  
  

* Hands-on with industrial protocols: Modbus TCP/RTU (function codes, register maps, byte order), OPC UA, and MQTT. Exposure to S7, FINS, MC, FOCAS, BACnet, EtherNet/IP, DNP3, IEC 61850 or IEC 60870-5-104 is a plus.
* Networking you can debug by hand: IP addressing and subnets, static vs DHCP, routing, VLANs, firewalls, VPNs, isolated or air-gapped plant networks, and Wireshark.
* Comfortable on Linux: the shell, systemd, journald, Nginx, permissions and sudo, package management, bash scripting.
* Basic IT/OT security principles: the Purdue model and network segmentation, IEC 62443 concepts, least privilege, secrets handling, and why you don't write to a running PLC without sign-off.
* Structured troubleshooting: you isolate the layer that's failing (wiring, device, protocol, network, service, cloud) instead of guessing.
* Clear written English. Your guides and site reports get read by people who weren't there, and often by people who aren't technical.
* Willing to travel to plants and work in panel rooms and on shop floors, roughly 30–40% of the time.

**Bonus Points**

* Has built a tool or internal product that non-technical people actually adopted, and iterated on it based on how they used it.
* Has written a protocol driver, or wrapped a vendor library, and run it against real hardware.
* Experience with Kafka/Redpanda, Prometheus/Grafana, React or TypeScript, CMake/vcpkg, or cross-compiling for ARM.
* CI/CD and packaging (Jenkins, offline installs for air-gapped sites).
* Comfortable using AI-assisted development to get up to speed on a new language or library quickly, and to close a gap while you're still on site.
* Has commissioned a system that actually went live and stayed live, or is an ex-automation, instrumentation or plant engineer who moved into software.
* Comfortable being told the panel is undocumented, the tag list is wrong and the network is flat, and getting it working anyway.

**Why Faclon?**
Industrial AI at real scale, across sectors and geographies. You own a platform that runs on real machines, not a demo. You decide which protocol it learns next and how easy it is for the next person to deploy. A small team where your judgment decides what ships, how it holds up in the field, and who can use it.

We are developing a mobile application that combines real-world interactions with location and proximity technologies. Our team uses AI coding tools and autonomous coding agents to accelerate development, improve engineering workflows, and share practical knowledge.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Mobile & Platform Engineer who can work across Android and iOS, contribute to our Kotlin Multiplatform architecture, and support our dedicated developers on both platforms.
  
  
Your main focus will be enabling the team to deliver effectively: resolving technical challenges, maintaining shared components, improving development workflows, and managing the backend and infrastructure that support the application.

* Support our Android and iOS developers with technical decisions, debugging, code reviews, and integration challenges.

* Manage server-side application deployments, configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
* Establish effective AI-assisted and agentic coding workflows across the team.
* Review AI-generated code and ensure that changes are tested, understandable, secure, and maintainable.
* Help developers and junior team members use AI tools effectively through practical demonstrations and knowledge sharing.
* Where appropriate, act as technical team lead: coordinate dependencies, guide implementation, review technical decisions, and help the team resolve blockers.

**Required Qualifications**

* Demonstrated senior-level experience in mobile software development.
* Strong Kotlin and Android development experience, together with practical Swift and iOS development experience.
* Solid hands-on experience with Kotlin Multiplatform and integrating shared code into both mobile platforms.
* The ability to investigate problems across mobile clients, APIs, backend services, databases, and infrastructure.
* Practical backend development experience and a sound understanding of API design, authentication, and application security.
* Strong SQL and relational database experience, including schema changes, migrations, and performance troubleshooting.
* Hands-on DevOps experience with Linux servers, application deployment, configuration, and operational troubleshooting.
* Excellent Git and GitHub knowledge, including pull requests, code reviews, branch workflows, and repository configuration.
* Strong experience with GitHub Actions and configuring and maintaining GitHub runners.
* Substantial experience using AI coding assistants and coding agents to deliver working software.
* The ability to establish development workflows that combine coding agents, automated checks, and human review.
* Clear communication, practical documentation skills, and a willingness to share knowledge.
* The ability to work independently while supporting other developers constructively.
* Interest in a long-term, full-time position and availability to start promptly after an agreement is reached.

**Especially Valuable Experience**

* Previous experience as a technical lead or senior engineer supporting a mobile development team.
* GPS, BLE, UWB, NFC, or other location and proximity technologies.
* Testing mobile applications on real devices and investigating platform-specific behavior.
* Container-based application deployment and reproducible development environments.
* Monitoring, incident diagnosis, and maintaining reliable backend services.
* Coordinating changes that affect mobile applications, backend APIs, and database structures together.

* A fully remote, full-time role with a long-term perspective.

* Support and mentor other developers and admins, sharing knowledge and helping raise technical standards across the team.

* Strong knowledge of Apex, Lightning Web Components, and SOQL/SOSL.
* Strong Salesforce configuration skills, including Flow, object modelling, validation rules, security, and sharing.
* Experience making or contributing meaningfully to technical design and architecture decisions, rather than only implementing predefined solutions.
* Experience integrating Salesforce with external systems using REST/SOAP APIs, platform events, or similar integration patterns.
* Strong understanding of automated testing, code quality, and code review practices.
* Experience working with Git\-based version control and modern Salesforce development and deployment practices.
* Ability to independently investigate and resolve complex technical or production issues.
* Strong communication skills, with experience working directly with technical and non\-technical stakeholders to understand problems, challenge assumptions, and explain technical trade\-offs clearly.
